Based on the Piper PA-28-181 Cherokee Archer II POHs VB-760 Rev. 5 (N9658K) and VB-790 (N5525V, S/N 28-7790481, with Supplement 3 AutoControl IIIB and the GDL 88 AFMS 190-01310-02), and the FPI Piper PA28 Checkout Form rev. 11/18/2026

items.prompt: N9658K: fly the inner (knot) ring. MPH in brackets is 58K's outer ring and arcs (VB-760).
Flaps lock and carry weight on the step only when fully up.
No oil pressure in 30 seconds: shut down. Limit cranking to 30 seconds with a 2 minute rest.
Warm up no more than 2 minutes in warm weather, 4 in cold. Avoid prolonged idling.
Differential 50 RPM maximum. One magneto no longer than 10 seconds.
Avoid prolonged ground operation with carburetor heat on: the air is unfiltered.
Lean above 5,000 ft, or lower at 75% power or less. Lean until rough, then enrich until smooth. In doubt below 5,000 ft: full rich.
Alternate tanks (VB-790: 1 hour, then 2 hours; VB-760: hourly). Fuel pump ON to switch, then OFF. Never run a tank dry.
In a long power off descent, clear the engine by opening and closing the throttle.
Full rich at low airports (POH). At high elevation airports set best power instead: full rich loses power for a go around.
Heat reduces power, which matters in a go around. Full throttle with heat on can cause detonation.
Refuel if >1 tach hr. since last fill.
Ice shows as a drop in RPM. Expect more roughness as it melts, then smoothness.
Complete loss may be oil exhaustion or a bad gauge. The engine may stop suddenly.
Turn on the landing light: no increase means the alternator has failed.
The OFF then ON resets the overvoltage relay. With ALT off the battery is the only power.
Rocker OFF or pull the AP breaker. Overpower at either wheel (POH Supplement 3).
A 3 second delay can give 45° bank and 180 ft lost; on approach, 1 second gives 18° and 10 ft.
Both open: side latch first, then top. 58K POH: open the top latch, push the door out, close it rapidly, latch the top.
Overpriming is the usual cause. If it starts, keep it running to pull the fire in.
After fuel exhaustion, power may take up to 10 seconds to return after switching tanks.
Lose excess altitude by widening the pattern, flaps or slips. Touch down at the lowest safe speed.
